questions.text: plugins/notifications/src/api/NotificationsClient.test.ts mocks the notifications backend with `setupServer()` and `http.get(...)` handlers instead of stubbing `fetchApi` or `fetch` directly. Why is the test written this way?

plugins/notifications/src/api/NotificationsClient.ts receives a `fetchApi` in its constructor (wired from `fetchApiRef` in src/plugin.ts) instead of importing an HTTP library such as node-fetch or cross-fetch. Why? Name the decision that applies today.
plugins/notifications/src/components/RelativeTime/RelativeTime.tsx handles timestamps with luxon's `DateTime` rather than Moment.js or a hand-written helper on `Date`. Why luxon?
Components in plugins/notifications/src/components (for example RelativeTime) are typed as plain functions taking a props object, never as `React.FC<Props>`. Why?

Each subfolder of plugins/notifications/src (api, hooks, components and each component folder) has its own index.ts, and src/index.ts re-exports from ./api, ./hooks and ./components instead of reaching into deeper files. Why is the package's public surface built through index files this way?
